subject: Precision Health — questions on LLM training, log retention, and evidence pack
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@precisionhealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick privacy questions re: hosted LLM usage

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo today. Before we proceed we'd like a short written summary for our security and privacy review. A few concrete questions so our InfoSec and Legal teams can triage: 

1) Does Redwood ever use customer prompts / responses to further train or finetune hosted models (i.e., "train on customer data")? If yes, under what conditions?
2) Do you offer an explicit "no-train" / "do not use for training" guarantee or flag per tenant? If so, is there an attestation we can include in our DPIA?
3) What is the retention policy for prompts, responses, and debug logs by default? Can retention be shortened and can we request deletion?
4) For customers in regulated health verticals (HIPAA scope), do you offer BAAs or a Private deployment option (VPC / on-prem)?
5) Can you provide SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts or a short evidence pack for our third-party risk team?

We're on a tight timeframe — could you share an evidence pack and any short attestation language by next week? I've attached our standard questionnaire for reference.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Security Ops
Precision Health

Attachment: precisionhealth_ai_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Quick privacy questions re: hosted LLM usage

Hi Elena — great questions and thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, longer follow-up folder to come: 

1) Training on customer data: By default, Redwood's hosted inference endpoint does not use customer prompts/responses to update model weights or to train models used for other customers. We operate a model catalog and do not perform cross-tenant training with customer content unless explicitly engaged under a separate data-science agreement.

2) No-train option: Yes — we offer a tenant-level "no-train" flag that prevents any customer content from being used for any form of model training or finetuning. For regulated customers we can provide a signed attestation.

3) Retention: Default retention for request/response logs and debug traces is 30 days for hosted customers; aggregated telemetry is retained longer for product quality. We can shorten retention windows or delete logs on request; we also expose deletion APIs and a formal erasure workflow.

4) HIPAA & Private deployment: We offer a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) and Dedicated GPU pools which are typically recommended for PH. We also execute BAAs for covered entities.

5) Evidence pack: We're assembling SOC2 summary, SIG/CAIQ mapping, our no-train attestation, and DPIA guidance. Marissa will upload the folder in ~3 business days; with Legal sign-off we can provide signed attestation in ~5 business days.

Next steps: I will share a Drive link with the evidence pack shortly. If helpful, we can set a 30-minute call to walk through the attachments and answer the questionnaire directly. Proposed times: Tue/Thu morning PT next week.

Attachments (initial): no-train_attestation.pdf (pdf), soc2-summary.pdf (pdf)

Regards,
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the rapid reply, that's helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our privacy team: 

- For the "no-train" mode, can you confirm whether any internal telemetry (for debugging/perf) may include hashed PII-derived tokens that would be accessible to data scientists? In short: in no-train mode, is there any path for PH customer content to show up in datasets used for model improvement or analysis?
- For hosted customers, is per-tenant logical isolation (separate KV namespaces / cache partitioning) guaranteed, or could two tenants share caching layers?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports pseudonymization (tokenization) at the edge before content reaches the model?

I've attached our questionnaire for your security team's line-by-line answers — could you have the completed spreadsheet back in 5 business days?

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: precisionhealth_ai_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@precisionhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: 2028-03-24T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick privacy questions re: hosted LLM usage

Elena — thanks for the follow-ups, answered inline below and including next steps: 

- No-train telemetry: In no-train mode we do not route tenant request/response content into training pipelines or shared datasets. Operational telemetry (error traces, sampling-based perf metrics) is aggregated and does not include raw customer content. We can also enable stricter masking of tokens in traces (e.g., redact PII before sending to Sentry/observability). If PH wants absolute assurance, our Private deployment or Dedicated pools prevent transit of content through shared observability endpoints.

- Cache / KV isolation: Hosted customers run on a multi-tenant runtime but with strict logical isolation: each tenant gets an isolated KV namespace and prefixing to ensure no cross-tenant key collisions. Shared caching layers are used at the infrastructure level for efficiency, but KV namespaces and access controls prevent cross-tenant reads. For the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated capacity or Private deployment (we include full isolation guarantees in those contracts).

- Pseudonymization at edge: We support optional pre-processing hooks and SDKs so customers can tokenise/pseudonymize content before it reaches our API. For PH we can provide integrations patterns or help implement an edge redaction layer.

Attachments: deployment-options-overview.pdf (pdf), dpia-next-steps.md (md)

Action items / timeline: 
- Marissa will upload a completed SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet and SOC2 summary within 3 business days.
- Legal review / signed no-train attestation & BAA comments: ~5 business days.
- If you want to explore Private deployment, I'll loop our Solutions Architect and schedule a deep-dive.

Would you like to set a call Wednesday or Friday morning PT?

Best,
Ben Carter
